To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the induction of apoptotic cell death in antigen presenting cells can either enhance or impair antigen presentation, depending on the cell death-inducing stimulus and the signaling pathway(s) involved.
apoptosis can impair CD1d-mediated presentation, but the mechanisms involved differ depending on the apoptotic stimulus
the induction of apoptotic cell death in antigen presenting cells can severely impair CD1d-mediated presentation of lipid antigens to natural killer T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of CD1d antigen presentation by apoptotic stimuli and the signal transduction pathways involved in such a regulation.
the regulation of CD1d antigen presentation in response to apoptosis induction.
the regulation of CD1d expression and antigen presentation in the context of apoptosis, and the possible consequences on the development of anti-tumor responses in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
caspase activation is a key factor that determines the fate of antigen presentation following the stimulation of apoptosis in APC.
caspase-3 is not required for the induction of apoptosis but is required for the inhibition of CD1-d mediated antigen presentation.
the induction of apoptotic cell death can severely compromise CD1d-mediated lipid antigen presentation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inhibition of topoisomerase-I activity and elevation of intracellular level of ceramide can induce the apoptosis of dendritic cells, and such an apoptosis could inhibit the CD1d-mediated antigens presentation.
the stimulation of apoptosis in antigen-presenting cells can severely impair the ability to present antigens via the CD1d molecule.
the induction of cell death in the context of antigen presenting cells can have profound consequences on CD1d antigen presentation.
